claim: V09 deleted the `crisis.look.<kind>` catalogue family this round (VV1112-r2-14): each look is worded by its `crisis.looks` row's `label` (V11 §3.25.9), and V09's repair handed the change to V10. Three V10 sites still name the family: §1.2's V09 row (l. 202: 'V09 §4.21.12: `crisis.look.<kind>`, `info.crisis.*` … whose words the clerk renders'), T-V10-29 (l. 3097: 'every `info.damage.*`, `info.crisis.*` and `crisis.look.<kind>` key V10 §3.9a and V10 §3.9b (8) render' has a catalogue key in every shipped locale) and CVR-V10-22 (l. 3449). claim: T-V10-52 (l. 3120) carries, by R3-09 (e), 'a fire calamity naming a district with its linked `reconstruction` condition'. By V08 §3.16 (7) (b) and DR44 that condition carries `event` `calamity`, reads the `disaster` row and is look-bearing, so it is public at every key. The test's knowledge clause still enumerates 'at `public` every look-bearing condition — the siege, the refugee wave and the plague — is listed', which misses the fourth look its own fixture stands. A test written from the enumeration either misses the disaster look or fails on it; the clause's 'lists exactly §11.2's `looks` answer's crises' decides, so the enumeration only misstates it.
required_change: T-V10-52: 'at `public` every look-bearing condition — the siege, the refugee wave, the plague and the fire's linked `reconstruction` condition (its disaster look) — is listed with its name and weeks (§7.7's DR44)'.

claim: V10 §3.23 row 26 (l. 2678) gives 'a layer off' the outcome 'layer visibility is view state and never filters a read, which admits by key'. By R3-21 (a), §8.4 and §7.4, layer visibility is `LayerSpec.visible`, the document's style state, written by a logged `setLayer`, the very event V10's own §4.1 T12 encoder writes (`setLayer { layer, spec: { visible } }`). The outcome that counts — a hidden layer never filters a read — is the same; the classification is the retired one.
required_change: V10 §3.23 row 26: 'layer visibility is view state and never filters a read, which admits by key' → 'layer visibility (`LayerSpec.visible`, the document's style state, written by a logged `setLayer`, §8.4) never filters a read, which admits by key'.

claim: V10 §2.13's `LookAnswer.festivals` (l.1000–1001) projects §11.2's `LooksAnswer.festivals`, its `name` commented "a dossier tradition's (V08 §3.16 (5)); a standalone generic festival, which it names not"; §3.9b (5) (l.1946–1948) calls it "the list V09 §4.21.8 reads"; T-V10-49 asserts `read_map look` returns "the festival list the view shows". But the base's `LooksAnswer.festivals` is "DR43's list" (l.16159) and DR43 holds "standalone no tradition exists and none is invented" (l.11980); V11's registry row 105 gives `festival.generic` to "V09's preview list, standalone" and the renderer directly (V11 l.1030); V09 §4.21.8 (1) lists the generic festivals standalone (T-V9-78: "standalone, the four generic festivals are listed"). On a standalone map the look read so returns no festival while the panel shows four, and T-V10-49 cannot pass against a base-conformant build. V10's round-3 HAND-OFFS name the gap; the base, V09 and V11 agree with each other, so V10 is the end that moves.
required_change: V10 §2.13's `name` comment reads "LooksAnswer's `name` — a dossier tradition's (V08 §3.16 (5)); the list is DR43's, so a standalone map's is empty (no tradition exists, DR43), a previewed generic festival (V11 §3.25.7's `festival.generic`) reaching the model only through `display.id`, rendered in V09's `view.festival.<id>` words"; §3.9b (5)'s "(`LooksAnswer.festivals`: §7.7's DR43, the list V09 §4.21.8 reads, under the session's key)" reads "(`LooksAnswer.festivals`: §7.7's DR43, the dossier's festivals V09 §4.21.8 lists, under the session's key; standalone none, a previewed generic festival named from the display)"; T-V10-49's "the festival list the view shows" reads "the dossier's festival list the view shows (§11.2's `LooksAnswer.festivals`), and on a standalone fixture no festival, a previewed generic one named in V09's words".
